seal.statement: Independent adversarial verification of the experimental raft-rs partition backend approved it with recorded defects and falsified none of the owner's five stop conditions, but it measured two that sit directly on the path the transport quest will take, and the owner has split them out as a prerequisite that must be independently approved before any real transport routing begins - because transport is precisely what introduces the caller paths that expose them, and proving transport first would leave its result ambiguous. The first is that the backend decides whether a failure was a WebAssembly fatal by asking whether the thrown value is an Error instance, while the boundary that asks encloses host JavaScript: every durable-store write in the Ready loop, the transport send hook, the address resolver that throws for a peer identity the local registry has not registered, and the application's own committed-entry callback. Measured twice by the verifier - closing a replica's SQLite handle retired the runtime and an unrelated group in it then refused dispatch, and a binding argument fault was called a fatal although no Rust ran - and reachable on the first real production write, which hands the core a JavaScript object where it needs bytes; the refusal branch of the repair this replaces has no test anywhere in the corpus. The second is that durable retirement gates the tick scheduler rather than the node, so a retired replica whose stale configuration still lists itself was driven directly through its own tick and raised the live cluster's term and cost it its leader, and admitted real envelopes besides; the property holds today only because the scheduler is the sole caller, which transport is about to stop being true. This quest fixes both and nothing else. It replaces the instance test with three structurally distinguished failure domains - a core refusal, which is a typed outcome of a normal raft-rs operation and never retires a runtime; a WebAssembly fatal, which is a trap or panic originating in the invocation itself or the binding's own explicit indication, and which marks its runtime unhealthy under the policy already recorded; and a host failure, which is JavaScript outside Rust and is neither of the others and carries its own recovery semantics - and it narrows the boundary that can classify a fatal to as close as practical around the invocation, so that persistence, sending, address resolution and application callbacks cannot be converted into a Raft-runtime fatal by throwing. Where the current surface leaves refusal and fatal ambiguous it changes the experimental binding minimally toward an unambiguous result rather than classifying exceptions more cleverly, and it resorts to matching a message only if the binding offers nothing stronger and a falsifier shows that adequate. It makes retirement an invariant of the node itself: a retired logical replica, after a restart and with no scheduler running, does not tick, campaign, accept inbound envelopes for active participation, originate traffic, accept proposals, or rejoin because stale local state still lists it, and the check happens before the core is touched rather than after, failing closed with a typed refusal. Retirement stays separate from the committed configuration, which continues to record what the node last knew about consensus membership while retirement records whether this local replica may participate at all, so retirement never rewrites the configuration and a retired identity is never reactivated by a later message. It does not resurrect the sender-membership rule an earlier evaluation falsified: for a replica that is not retired, inbound traffic still follows the corrected ingress semantics and a sender absent from the local applied configuration is still admitted. Its falsifiers are driven, not argued - each of the seven failure shapes the owner named, asserting the classification and whether the group, the runtime and unrelated groups remain usable; and the verifier's exact retirement reproducer, with the check then deliberately bypassed so the old disruptive behaviour reappears as a permanent load-bearing control. The apply-rollback invariant, outbound encoding, the committed-entry callback shape, the shared runtime singleton and the unregistered-peer workflow rule are recorded as inputs to the transport quest and are not absorbed here.

text: Lead ruling on the binding question phase 1 answered. MEASURED: the binding already makes a core refusal structurally distinguishable from a trap on the JavaScript side - jserr is JsValue::from_str and is the only Err constructor in the whole file, used 69 times with no other, so every refusal the binding can produce crosses as a string primitive and never as an Error, while a genuine raft-rs fatal arrives as a WebAssembly.RuntimeError. The owner's section 2 authorises exactly this: derive a structural discriminator from the binding, or change the binding to expose one. It is derivable, so we derive it and do NOT rebuild the wasm. The rule for phase 2 is therefore: a thrown string is a core refusal, a RuntimeError is a WASM fatal, anything else is a host failure - and after the boundary narrowing host JavaScript is outside the invocation in any case. This is not message-string matching, which the owner allowed only as a last resort: nothing depends on what a refusal says, only on what type it is. The implementer's caveat is accepted and its mitigation is required: the string tag is implicit, so one future js_sys::Error would silently reclassify a refusal as a host failure, and the receipt must therefore parse vendor/raft-rs-wasm/src/lib.rs and assert that every Err goes through jserr and that jserr is JsValue::from_str, so the discriminator is derived from the binding and breaks loudly rather than silently if the binding changes. The declared alternative - jserr returning a tagged object, one function changed and 69 call sites untouched - is recorded as available and cheap if the owner later wants the contract declared rather than derived; it costs a wasm rebuild with its thermal gate, digest and build-recipe updates, and is not taken now. The glue-thrown TypeError from proposing a non-byte value is left classifying as a host failure with no binding change, which is correct: it is neither the binding's Err nor a Rust trap. It is the shape the earlier verifier measured being called a fatal although no Rust ran, and receipt 6 drives it.

Three binding-level findings phase 1 recorded rather than absorbed (R17), all outside this quest's two boundaries and all inputs to the transport quest. ONE, and the most serious: proposing a JavaScript object does not throw - the generated glue reads its length as undefined and uint8_to_vec produces a zero-length command, so the core receives an EMPTY proposal. On a follower it surfaces as a dropped proposal, which is what the earlier verifier saw and reported as a misclassification, but on a leader it would commit an empty entry. partition-service-raft-write-commit.js:37 hands the provider exactly such an object, so this is the first real production write on this backend. This is worse than the misclassification it was found behind: it is silent acceptance of a malformed proposal rather than a refusal, and it belongs to the parked outbound-encoding item with that severity attached. TWO: a wrong-typed handle silently reaches another group, because the generated glue coerces the u32 argument and a string coerces to zero, so a caller passing a bad handle drives whatever group holds handle zero; negative and fractional handles are refused. THREE: a trap's measured blast radius is narrower than the recorded policy assumes - after the panic the trapping group's handle is gone from the binding's table, because the call had removed it and the abort skipped the re-insert, so that group answers invalid handle while the rest of the runtime still works and an unrelated create_node succeeds on the same instance. The recorded policy of retiring the whole runtime stands; the measured fact is that the trapped group's in-memory state is the part actually lost.

Phase 2 (both boundaries) by the same Opus implementer under the owner's prerequisite addendum; probe 11 to 0, all thirteen receipts green, three commits since the seal each through the real pre-commit hook with no baseline raised. D1: the Error-instance discriminator is deleted and three named failure domains replace it in production - a thrown string is a core refusal because the binding's jserr is its only Err constructor and is JsValue::from_str, a WebAssembly.RuntimeError is a WASM fatal, anything else is a host failure - and nothing anywhere reads a message. The classifying boundary is narrowed structurally rather than by discipline: the runtime host hands work a guarded facade whose every primitive is its own invocation with its own panic-capture window, a throw there is re-thrown tagged, and the outer catch treats anything untagged as a host failure BY CONSTRUCTION, so a durable-store write, a send hook, an address resolver or an application callback cannot reach the fatal branch because nothing else could have raised the tag. Only an invocation retires a runtime. The derivation is protected as the lead required: receipt 1 parses the binding source at the path production itself resolves and requires jserr to be exactly JsValue::from_str, that constructor to occur once in the crate, every Err to come through jserr, and no JsError, js_sys::Error or JsValue::from anywhere - and it falsifies itself in the same test against three mutated copies of the real source, each asserted to differ from it, so the parse cannot pass by comparing a file with itself. All eight shapes driven on the real core, each recording origin, own-group usability, runtime health, unrelated-group usability and recovery: an ordinary refusal and a binding argument rejection are core refusals leaving everything usable and the refusal retryable once the precondition the core named holds; a SQLite failure after a successful call, a send hook throwing with real messages in hand, an address resolver throwing through the production node, an application callback throwing, and the glue-thrown argument fault are all host failures with the runtime healthy; a genuine Rust panic is the only fatal, and replaceRuntime recovers it. Recorded rather than repaired inside receipt 6, as instructed: for the JavaScript object production actually hands the provider the binding does NOT reject the argument as the owner's shape list assumed - propose completes, origin is null, the core commits the entry and the application is handed nothing, because the committed entry carries no data. D2: one lifecycle owner reads the durable retirement record at construction, before a tick driver exists and before any message can arrive, and the node has a single admission guard every active call passes through first - tick, propose, ingest before the envelope boundary and therefore before step, and drain, which was the last reachable unguarded path; reads stay open so a retired replica may still be inspected, and campaign is refused through the same lifecycle so there is one retirement fact in the process rather than two. The ordering is proved rather than described: after retiring, the group's handle is freed with the core's own primitive, so any call that reached the core could only answer invalid handle, and the node still answers replica-retired. The verifier's exact reproducer is driven end to end on a real three-replica partition through the real seam - partitioned, removed, stale local configuration still listing itself, retirement recorded, restarted with a recording clock never asked to schedule anything, then sixty direct ticks and real envelopes captured off the transport from the live leader before delivery, never hand-written - all refused, no outbound packet with the transport emptied first, the retired replica's own core term unmoved and the leading replica's term and believed leader unchanged. The bypass control now goes round the node entirely, since the node has no unguarded path left, and the live leader's term rises and it loses its leader, so the green cannot pass vacuously. Retirement never rewrites the configuration: the stale configuration and the durable voters row are byte-for-byte unchanged across retirement and restart, the identity is the same, and later envelopes change neither the record nor the refusal; the ingress guard looks only at this replica's lifecycle and never at the sender, and the membership-race receipt stayed green throughout, so the falsified sender rule has not returned. No binding change and no rebuild - the vendored tree is byte-identical since the seal, confirmed by the lead. Method disclosure: the production changes were driven by the phase-1 reds, but the binding parse and the narrowing control were added after the implementation on the lead's instruction and are not claimed test-first, each carrying its own driven falsifier; and while making the reds green the implementer found three of its own phase-1 drives were not exercising what they claimed, because the red had stopped earlier in the test, and two retirement measurements used the wrong instrument - all five corrected and reported. Liferaft unchanged and still the default: 89 of 89 raft files and 105 of 105 partition files green.

Independent adversarial verification at HEAD 736ec7e75: REJECT. NEITHER property is affirmed - failure origin is not correctly classified, and retirement does not hold regardless of caller path - so under the owner's section 10 transport does not start. The headline, which the lead confirmed directly: both boundaries are soundly built where they exist and the verifier could not break either from inside, but the production provider seam is outside both. raft-rs-node.js raftRsGroupParts returns core: this.host.core, the UNGUARDED runtime, and raft-rs-provider.js resolves every node through it, so provider propose, shutdownNode, getCurrentTerm, getCommittedIndex and the partition control's campaign all reach the core with no classifying boundary and no admission guard. Measured through that seam on a restarted, retired replica: sixty raw ticks accepted with the replica's own core term moving 1 to 5, a campaign accepted, a step accepted, and a proposal accepted - the last being the literal production write at partition-service-raft-write-commit.js:37, with has_ready moving false to true and the freed-handle instrument proving it reaches the core. A genuine Rust panic driven through that same seam throws at the caller and leaves the runtime healthy, and the aftermath is then misreported as an ordinary core refusal with the message invalid handle, so a group retired by a trap is indistinguishable from one that merely refused. Also blocking: a core refusal escapes provider propose as a bare string whose message is undefined, which every catch in the partition service reads. Ordering: raft-rs-election-safety.js reads core.status at line 44 before testing retirement at line 46, and with the handle freed the campaign path throws the core's invalid handle instead of the typed refusal - the lead confirmed the line ordering. What HELD under attack: every one of the owner's host-failure shapes was refused the fatal classification, including a SQLite error deliberately re-thrown as a RuntimeError from host code; the fatal tag could not be raised from outside an invocation, the untagged-means-host claim holding by construction; the panic capture window is per-invocation with no cross-attribution and console.error restored; the guarded facade covers all nineteen reachable core names with none unguarded; the binding parse is load-bearing, going red on three real mutations of the vendored source and green on the unmutated control; the free instrument is real; twelve of thirteen receipts go red when the thing they claim is broken in a copy, including both that had been red only at a naming gate; liferaft is still the default and unchanged; the vendored binding is byte-identical with no rebuild; no ratchet moved; and the membership-race property itself holds, the verifier driving a genuine vote request from a peer absent from the receiver's applied configuration and seeing it admitted, so the falsified sender rule has not returned. NEW FINDINGS about the binding and the core, non-blocking: a WASM stack-exhaustion trap arrives as a RangeError rather than a RuntimeError and is therefore classified host with the runtime left healthy - a genuine fatal downgraded, the direction section 4 forbids, and reachable at the call depths transport introduces; a string thrown by host code running inside an invocation, through the glue's own property read, is classified a core refusal, which is safe but lies about origin; the binding parse misses a refusal built in a map_err closure from a non-string JsValue, which would cross as a host failure; and nothing binds the vendored source to the built artifact, the digest sealing the artifact alone, so the parse is a proxy rather than a seal. HARNESS defects: receipt 12 is vacuous - none of its three envelopes actually come from the absent sender, and reintroducing a sender-membership filter leaves it green, so the receipt guarding the owner's blocking clause proves nothing even though the property holds; and receipt 7's instrument does not distinguish a check made before the core from one made after and overriding, since moving the guard after the work left it green, though receipt 8 catches that. EVALUATION-CLAIM defects in the attempt record: the node does have unguarded active paths - raftRsGroupParts, drainAdmitted, send, end and the host data member; drain is guarded but drainAdmitted is not and is reachable, running the whole Ready loop on a retired replica; send originates a real packet from one; and the bypass control does not go round the node, using five of its members. Not verified: that the pre-commit hook ran unbypassed on each commit. The ten raft-suite failures reproduce identically at the seal and are pre-existing.

CORRECTION to the phase-2 attempt record at 736ec7e75, which the verifier found overclaimed. Three of its statements were false as written and are withdrawn. FIRST, 'the node has no unguarded active path' was false: raftRsGroupParts handed out core: this.host.core - the unguarded runtime itself - and drainAdmitted, send and end were all reachable, so the node had several. SECOND, 'drain was the last one' was false for the same reason and because drainAdmitted, which runs the whole Ready loop, sat right behind the guarded drain. THIRD, 'the bypass control goes round the node entirely' was false: it used five node members - host, key, store, groupId and send - so it went through the node rather than round it. What is true at HEAD now: raftRsGroupParts hands out no core and no handle at all, only three named ways to reach one, all inside the classifying boundary and the active one inside the admission boundary as well; there is a single drain and it asks; send asks, because originating a packet is taking part; end asks by way of a teardown decision the lifecycle owner admits by name, so that refusing would not leak the handle retirement tells the host to release; and the bypass control now uses the group's classifying path and the partition's own request send hook, with no node member at all. The earlier claims were made from reading the node's own methods rather than from the census of what production reaches through the seam, which is exactly the gap the verifier measured.

RECORDED, NOT FIXED (owner ruling: record, do not fix), three findings the independent verifier made about the binding and the derivation, all outside the two boundaries this quest repairs. ONE: a string thrown by HOST JavaScript running inside an invocation - through the generated glue's own property read, for instance - is classified a core refusal rather than a host failure. It is safe in the direction that matters, since it never becomes a fatal and never retires a runtime, but it lies about origin, and the reason is structural: the discriminator is the thrown value's type, and host code is free to throw a string. Making it exact would need the binding to tag its own refusals, which is the declared alternative the owner recorded as available and cheap (jserr returning a tagged object, one function changed, 69 call sites untouched) and did not take. TWO: the binding parse that makes the derivation load-bearing checks that every Err is constructed from jserr and that jserr is JsValue::from_str, but it does not catch a refusal built inside a map_err closure from a non-string JsValue; such a refusal would cross as a host failure rather than as a core refusal. The parse is therefore a strong proxy and not a complete one. THREE: nothing binds the vendored crate source to the built artifact. artifact-digest.json seals the .wasm and the glue, and the parse reads src/lib.rs, but no check proves that this source is what produced that artifact, so the derivation rests on a proxy rather than a seal. Closing it needs either a reproducible-build check or a source digest recorded at build time, which is binding-provenance work and belongs with whoever next rebuilds the artifact.

Repair answering the independent rejection, by the same Opus implementer; all seven items, probe back to metric 0 with thirteen receipts, three commits each through the real hook with no baseline raised. The seam is closed more strongly than the verifier proposed: raftRsGroupParts now hands out NO core and NO handle at all, returning a group handle carrying identity plus exactly three named ways to reach the core, all inside the classifying boundary - admitted, which asks the lifecycle owner first and is what everything taking part in the group uses; classified, the invocation boundary alone, for reads; and teardown for freeing. The lead confirmed the returned object carries no raw core or handle. The justification is sound and worth recording: the defect was that a caller could obtain the raw runtime through the node, so the repair removes the raw runtime from what the node hands out rather than adding a check beside it - with a guarded facade beside a raw one a future caller can reconstruct the old path, with no core on the object it cannot - and the receipt asserts that absence structurally. Provider propose now goes through admitted, shutdownNode through teardown, the term and committed-index reads through classified, and the partition control's campaign through admitted with the election owner naming the refusal in its own vocabulary so the provider contract is unchanged. The verifier's four seam attacks - raw tick, campaign, step and the literal production write - are permanent controls driven on a restarted retired replica every run, and afterwards the core is asked what it was given, with has_ready and the term both required unmoved. Election ordering fixed and confirmed by the lead: the retirement test is now first, before the core is touched, taking the peer id from the caller because the caller is the replica, so the freed-handle instrument gets the typed refusal instead of the core's invalid handle. drainAdmitted is gone from src entirely, confirmed by the lead - there is one drain and it asks; send asks, because originating a packet is taking part; and the bypass control now genuinely goes round the node, reaching the core through the classifying path and sending through the partition's own request hook, using no node member. A disclosed deviation the lead ACCEPTS: end asks the lifecycle through teardown, which ADMITS by name, because refusing to free a retired replica's handle would leak the very resource retirement tells the host to release and freeing takes no part in the group - it can originate nothing; that is a recorded decision rather than an omission, and R13's bounded resource lifetime supports it. A stack-exhaustion trap arriving as a RangeError rather than a RuntimeError is now classified a fatal when it happens in an invocation, with the opposite direction driven in the same receipt so host code that recurses away its own stack stays host; the drive searches for the depth band rather than declaring it, sweeping four primitives because how much JavaScript the glue runs inside one call sets the band's width, and the implementer disclosed honestly that a single primitive gives a band about one frame wide that its first two drives stepped over. Receipt 12 is no longer vacuous: it empties the transport, ticks the removed non-retired replica until it originates traffic of its own, and requires the fed-back envelope to be FROM that replica while the receiver's applied configuration does not list it, so a reintroduced sender filter goes red by construction. Receipt 7's control is deliberate now: beside the freed-handle instrument the core is asked what it was given, so a guard moved after the work leaves has_ready and the term moved - the verifier's own instrument made permanent. A provider refusal no longer escapes as a bare string: the seam converts a named outcome into an Error subclass carrying a message, which every partition-service catch reads, plus the outcome and origin so a caller branches on the domain rather than on text. The attempt record's three false claims are withdrawn by name in an appended entry, with the reason recorded - they were written from the node's own methods rather than from a census of what production reaches through the seam. Recorded and not fixed: the in-invocation host string classified as a core refusal; the binding parse missing a non-string refusal built in a map_err closure; and nothing binding the vendored source to the built artifact. Lead's own note for the next verifier: the doc comment above raftRsGroupParts still says it returns core and handle and is now stale; and the node still exposes host and key, which together equal the classified path, deliberately and with no production caller, which the next adversarial pass should test.

Independent adversarial verification round 2 at HEAD 26a081162: REJECT. Neither property affirmed, so under the addendum's section 10 transport does not start. This is the SECOND consecutive rejection on the same root: the guards are applied at named paths while the raw runtime stays transitively reachable one level deeper. Round 1 rejected because raftRsGroupParts returned core and handle as fields; the repair removed those fields and the receipt asserts their absence, but the object still carries host and key, and the lead confirmed that RaftRsRuntimeHost exposes a public core getter and a public handleOf, so parts.host.core with parts.host.handleOf(parts.key) is the raw unguarded runtime and the handle. Measured on a restarted RETIRED replica: sixty raw ticks accepted and its own term moved 1 to 12; driving sixty more with the Ready loop through the partition's own send hook took the LIVE cluster's term from 1 to 16 and its believed leader to zero - the live cluster lost its leader to a retired, restarted replica. Two further routes on the same object: classified takes arbitrary work and hands it the guarded core, so tick, campaign, step and the literal production write all completed on a retired replica; and teardown, which the lead confirmed calls admitTeardown, discards the answer and delegates to classified, so it runs arbitrary work and is a name rather than a constraint - tick, campaign and propose all reached the core through it. The verifier's judgment, which the lead accepts: classified is a general-purpose active path wearing a read's name, and the repository's own receipt 11 proves it by using classified AS its bypass control - a deliberate bypass that is a shipped public method of the object the provider resolves is not a bypass, it is the hole. Admitting a retired replica's free is not contested; restricting teardown to freeing is. A NEW defect the repair introduced: a host RangeError raised inside an invocation is now classified a WASM fatal and retires the shared process-wide runtime, while the same host code throwing an Error is host and throwing a string is a core refusal - so origin is still decided by the thrown value's JavaScript type, which constraint origin-not-type and section 1 forbid, and the repair fixed the downgrade section 4 forbids by introducing the reciprocal upgrade it also forbids. The source comment asserting host code cannot reach that branch is false. Production reachability of that upgrade is NOT VERIFIED - the driven route was a getter that real decoded envelopes would not present - but a production-plausible route exists in the glue's own allocations. Also false as measured: the election owner's comment that its primitive cannot be reached by calling the core directly. WHAT IS REPAIRED AND HELD: drainAdmitted is gone from the tree entirely; send on a retired replica produces no packet and real envelopes are refused; the election ordering fix is real, with the freed-handle instrument now answering the typed retirement refusal instead of the core's invalid handle; a provider refusal is now an Error subclass with a real message, outcome and origin; through the GUARDED paths a genuine panic is classified, retires the runtime and reports its aftermath honestly. Receipt 12 is no longer vacuous, confirmed two ways - the fed-back envelope really is from the absent peer and a reintroduced sender filter turns it red. Receipt 7's new control bites: moving the guard after the work turns it red where round 1 left it green. ALL THIRTEEN receipts now bite, against thirteen targeted production mutations, where round 1 found twelve. The RangeError band was reproduced independently across four primitives with the unreachable case failing loudly with a census rather than passing quietly. Probe honest, byte-identical on regeneration including the witness digests. Liferaft still the default; both suites green through the project's own runner - and round 1's ten raft failures are RECONCILED as the known mixed-runner trap, the file importing the project's tap helper rather than node:test, so they are not a regression. No ratchet moved, the vendored binding byte-identical with no rebuild, nothing outside the backend family changed. MATERIAL FOR THE OWNER'S DECISION: the verifier found NO current production caller that bypasses - production as written reaches the core only through guarded paths - so the defect is structural and latent rather than live, and the transport quest is precisely the new caller the addendum's section 5 says the invariant must survive. Fix shape named: classified takes a named read rather than a callback; teardown takes no callback and frees; the group handle and the node stop exposing host and key; the runtime host's core and handleOf stop being public; and receipt 8's absence assertion becomes transitive reachability rather than two property names at depth one.

Owner constraints added 2026-09-21 after the second rejection, keeping the current scope. Recorded as binding decisions rather than a reseal: the quest was sealed at a41990bb5 and each of these strengthens a sealed receipt while weakening none. ONE, result provenance over exception classification. The target is not to inspect a thrown object and decide its domain, but that the boundary which invoked the core already knows which domain produced the outcome: host preparation, then an invocation returning an explicit core-ok, core-refused or core-trap, then host persistence, sending and applying. A host JavaScript exception must never pass through the core classifier at all. If wasm-bindgen prevents exactly that shape, the reason is recorded and the smallest binding-level discriminator necessary is exposed. No extensible error taxonomy: the three domains are enough. This is the structural answer to the defect round 2 found, where origin was still decided by the thrown value's JavaScript type, and it resolves both halves at once - the RangeError upgrade disappears because host code never reaches the classifier, not because a type test was widened. TWO, retirement is one gate rather than guards copied onto methods. No separate checks inside tick, campaign, step, propose and configuration changes; one internal active-runtime gate that every core-entering path uses, and the invariant stated so it is mechanically enumerable - every production path that can invoke this RawNode first passes the same local lifecycle eligibility owner. The evidence script censuses all RawNode entry sites, and a newly added entry method in future makes the census red until it is routed through the gate. This is the mechanism that stops the defect recurring: two rejections have now found the guard applied at named paths while the raw runtime stayed reachable one level deeper, and a census of entry sites catches by construction what a check on two property names at depth one cannot. THREE, retirement and temporary unavailability stay distinct. Retired must not become a generic do-not-touch-Raft state: a retired logical replica is terminal for that identity, while not ready, transport unavailable, node draining, a local runtime restarting and a WASM runtime replacement must not mutate durable retirement. A falsifier is required showing a temporarily unavailable but non-retired replica resuming under the same logical identity, and conversely that a retired identity does not resume after restart merely because its old configuration still contains it. FOUR, runtime retirement is never the response to a host error, where the two defects interact. Only a genuine core fatal may invoke the trap policy. A host failure - SQLite unavailable, a packet send failing, an address lookup failing, an application callback failing - must not indirectly mark the RawNode retired, the logical replica retired, or the whole runtime unhealthy. Three separate concepts: logical replica retirement, Raft group or runtime failure, and host operation failure. A cross-product falsifier is required: a SQLite write throwing classifies as a host failure with the logical replica still non-retired, the runtime still healthy and recovery left to the storage owner; and a genuine fatal classifies as a core fatal making the runtime unhealthy WITHOUT the logical replica thereby becoming durably retired, because a trap kills an execution container and does not semantically remove a replica from the cluster.

Owner final rules 2026-09-21, keeping the existing seal and treating these as binding strengthening decisions; a reseal happens only if implementation proves a sealed acceptance criterion itself must change. ONE, the RawNode-entry census is the authority for closing the retirement property. Built before production changes, it enumerates every production-reachable path that can cause an operation on a RawNode or raft-rs handle INCLUDING INDIRECT PATHS, covering at least tick, step, campaign, propose, configuration-change proposals, status and progress reads where they expose a raw or mutable handle, teardown and free, and any generic classified, withNode, handleOf or callback path that can execute against the core. It is discovered from the adapter and runtime surface rather than maintained as a hand-written list of known method names wherever that is possible. The acceptance invariant: every production path that can enter the core crosses exactly one lifecycle-eligibility gate first, and no core capability is reachable around that gate. The census must be RED on the current implementation before repair, and after repair no raw handle, no host object containing a raw handle, no callback capable of arbitrary core invocation and no generic give-me-the-core accessor may cross the public backend seam; a future RawNode entry added without the gate turns it red. TWO, bypasses are not solved by renaming or nesting. Rounds one and two proved property-name checks insufficient, so a repair that merely turns host.core into host.parts.core or another nested or private-looking path is INVALID. The capability itself must become inaccessible, with closure or private-module ownership of the handle preferred, and the public node object exposing semantic operations rather than access to the underlying RawNode. THREE, one eligibility owner. No retirement check copied into each public method: one authoritative predicate, conceptually assertCoreEntryAllowed of an operation kind, owning durable retirement and local runtime lifecycle eligibility and NOT membership decisions, readiness, node health or transport sender membership. Every core-entering operation routes through it and the census proves it mechanically. FOUR, three independent states preserved: the logical replica lifecycle, where retired is durable and terminal for that identity; the Raft execution-container health, which a fatal changes without retiring the replica; and the host-operation outcome, which by occurring changes neither. Cross-product tests prove the independence. FIVE, provenance by construction rather than a better classifier: host preparation, then the invocation, then a structured core result, then host persistence, sending and applying, with host callbacks executing OUTSIDE the invocation boundary so only the invocation can produce a refusal or a trap and host code produces host failure. If wasm-bindgen makes a Rust refusal and a true trap indistinguishable, the smallest binding change necessary distinguishes them; reliance on instanceof, message text or stack format is allowed only if no stronger boundary literally exists, and then recorded and adversarially tested. SIX, the API stays small: three origin classes, core-refused, core-fatal and host-failure, with semantic refusal reasons allowed underneath the first but not standardised here. What matters is who produced the outcome and which recovery domain it affects. SEVEN, retirement survives every caller shape: the permanent falsifier bypasses the scheduler, the transport driver and the normal lifecycle wrapper, and after restarting a durably retired replica whose stale configuration still lists itself it attempts every publicly reachable active operation - tick, campaign, propose, configuration proposal and inbound envelope - all failing BEFORE core invocation, with a core-entry counter asserted to remain zero; then a mutant removes the gate and the disruptive behaviour must return. EIGHT, temporary unavailability must not look retired: a non-retired replica whose runtime or host substrate is temporarily unavailable - a transient SQLite failure, runtime reconstruction after a trap, transport lost and restored - recovers under the same logical identity, with durable retirement still false and no new identity minted merely because the execution container failed.
